mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent decline in real GDP over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods following two consecutive quarters of declining real GDP.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production index by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the industrial production index increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals a strengthening demand side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods where both housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls decrease by more than 100,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index over three consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods following three consecutive months of increasing consumer price index.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and real GDP growth is negative, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy coupled with economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods where the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and real GDP growth is negative.
